source: Two candidate lists supplied by the owner on 2026-10-22: a hand-checked scan by a friend (source 'friend') and 28 parallel GitHub scans by an assistant (source 'scan'), merged and re-checked once. Status and notes were written by the people who made the lists; none of the candidates was run by this project when this file was written.

status_meaning.ready: the lists call it ready for a first run
status_meaning.fixable: usable after a path or folder is corrected (the corrected path is in target_script)
status_meaning.risky: needs data or a network at run time, or writes into the repository
status_meaning.excluded: the lists exclude it (wrong script, cluster-only, needs a server)

excluded_without_entry: causalNLP/causal-agent (the command is a data download script)
SunilgarGusai/PAPER-JCMM-reproducibility (link to a published paper not verified)
Shifty, Re: Fairness Guarantees under Demographic Shift (original repository not found)

candidates.notes: Fixed seed, synthetic data, no download. The demo prints one result (fdr, tpr, fpr, shd, nnz); which table of the paper it matches is not verified. python-igraph may need a C core on some systems. The arXiv id was not in the list and was added by this project.

Writes its output into the repository by default (run_BnpC.py line 167); the repository is read-only in the sandbox, so -o <directory> is required. Seed by --seed. Pins Bottleneck 1.3.5, pandas 1.5.0, scikit-learn 1.5.0, scipy 1.10.1, seaborn 0.12.0; Python 3.9 to 3.11, not 3.8.
One step after the install. 44 MB; training may be heavy. Whether it writes into the repository is not checked.
The README calls it a toy example. Whether it writes into the repository is not checked.
The README lists the commands under the headings Table 1 and Table 2, so the table of each command is stated. Whether it writes into the repository is not checked.
One YAML configuration. Whether the data split downloads external data was not clear from the README.
Needs an environment variable (PYTHONPATH) before the command; it must go into the run setup.
The first list gave --dry-run, which lists and runs nothing. The README has a smoke test (about 6 s, real output); the full sweep is 315 runs, 15 to 20 min. Needs cd research.
The install runs bash install-antibody-lib.sh (network, install phase only). The ackley20c command needs no extra data.

Three copies exist: code/brittle-fracture, code/rayleigh-benard, code/shallow-water. The rayleigh-benard example downloads data from Zenodo (network); the other two generate data with Dedalus. The folder in target_script is provisional (the first of the two that need no download); the choice is open.
Synthetic data, no network. The command is run after cd into the folder.
The README says results can vary by 1 to 2 percent between identical runs. Needs cd model. The CUB data is not checked.
Needs cd code and a real dataset name instead of the placeholder.
MNIST is probably downloaded by torchvision on the first run (network).
The graph and data files must be downloaded by hand from Google Drive.
Image collection and pose data must be downloaded by hand from Google Drive.
The command needs --test_dataset CropDisease, an external benchmark downloaded by hand.
A separate download_data.sh fetches the data; visualisation is tied to Neptune.ai (probably not required to run).
CIFAR10 is probably downloaded on the first run (network).
The default dataset (Enron) may need a download; pyg_lib and torch_scatter are platform-specific builds.
Needs bert-base-uncased weights and the GLUE data from Hugging Face (network).
The README says to unzip the data into the repository, so it writes into the repository, which is read-only in the sandbox.
A separate step (save_pca_and_ica_embeddings.py) must run first; GloVe vectors probably must be downloaded.
The README says the datasets are downloaded automatically from the internet; the data must be cached beforehand.

Two commands in order: the first prepares the data, the second runs the experiment. The author warns that the seed is fixed but differs from the paper's, so results will be somewhat different from the paper's.
The script is not this paper's code: RecAI is a vendored copy of another project with its own terms. The paper's own code is in eval/ and analysis/ and needs data from Google Drive.
The command analyses logs; the experiment itself is train.sh, which needs prepared feature files.
Designed for a SLURM cluster and Singularity containers, not a single Docker run.
A separate SPARQL server must run first (http://localhost:8890/sparql).
